perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s available perspective:

- She knows she is Sara Manuelito, a Speech-Language Pathologist; Shirley Whiteplume is her long-time colleague, close friend, and a nurse at their community health center.
- She attended the funeral of a patient she and Shirley shared. She observed Shirley looking somber and thought Shirley was deeply affected. Sara told Shirley she had seen how much Shirley cared; she heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept thinking if more could have been done. Sara said they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought; Shirley said Sara was right but letting go was hard.
- During a coffee break, Sara raised the treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley appreciated it but said it was hard to accept.
- In their office, Sara observed Shirley being reserved and minimally expressive. Sara told her it was okay to be open. Shirley said she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said expressing emotion does not make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try.
- Later, Sara felt her earlier confrontation might have been too harsh and apologized. Shirley said it was a bit much but that Sara meant well, and she appreciated the apology. Sara offered support; Shirley thanked her and said talking helps.
- Later, Sara noticed Shirley seemed improved and felt hopeful. She asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she was better, thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work; Shirley agreed to plan something for the weekend.

Sara has access only to these observed behaviors, heard statements, her own actions, and her own thoughts/feelings. She does not have access to Shirley’s unspoken thoughts or private information beyond what Shirley stated or showed.
